To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stochastic heavy ball (SHB) method with fixed stepsize and momentum term is a linearly convergent method for minimizing the expected loss of a generalization error, that the SHB method with fixed step size and momentum term is also a linearly converging method for minimizing a strongly convex expected loss, and that the SHB with momentum term and fixed step size can be applied for minimizing the expected risk of a generalization loss with quadratic loss function.
(i) the stochastic heavy ball algorithm converges at a rate of O(1/k), and (ii) the rate of convergence can be accelerated to O(1/k2) by a proper choice of the stepsize and momentum.
The heavy ball method converges with rate $O\bigl(1/k^{3/4}\bigr)$ for minimizing the expected generalization loss of linear regression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: Minimize the expected loss of a stochastic convex function.
the following question: can we obtain a linear convergence rate for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) methods, without any additional assumptions on the loss function?
the following question: Can the stochastic heavy ball momentum be used to improve the convergence of stochastic gradient descent for minimizing generalization loss?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stochastic heavy ball (SGD with momentum) method converges linearly to the optimal solution of the problem, provided the learning rate is sufficiently small, and the noise level is small enough.
the heavy ball momentum term is not a panacea.
the stochastic heavy ball algorithm converges linearly to an approximate solution of the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we show linear convergence for the heavy ball method for the first time, and we do so for minimizing generalization loss.
the method converges linearly to an optimal solution for minimizing the expected loss of a convex and possibly non-strongly convex function.
we prove linear convergence for a very simple algorithm, without the need of a line search, for minimizing the expected loss of general neural networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
linear convergence can be established for a much broader class of objectives than what has been previously considered.
the heavy ball momentum term can be used to speed-up the convergence rate of SGD in the stochastic setting, even for generalization error.
, under the right conditions, stochastic heavy ball can converge linearly to the optimum.
